sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: A beach village that receives a few hundred visitors a week treats them as guests. The same village receiving several thousand a day must treat them as a load: on its water supply, its roads, its waste collection and its patience. The visitors have not changed. What has changed is the ratio between what arrives and what the place can absorb, and planners call the upper limit of that ratio the carrying capacity.

The idea is simple to state and awkward to apply. A village does not have one limit but several, and they are reached at different times. The road may jam long before the wells run low; the beach may feel crowded to a resident and pleasantly lively to a shack owner. Whoever sets the number is therefore making a choice about whose discomfort counts. For this reason carrying capacity is better understood as a negotiated figure than as a measured one.

None of this makes the exercise pointless. A panchayat that knows its waste plant can handle four tonnes a day has a firm reason to refuse the licence that would bring a fifth. A figure of that kind does not settle every dispute, but it changes the question from whether growth is good to what must be built before more of it is allowed. Places that skip the calculation usually discover their limit anyway. They find it in the dry tap in April or the uncollected heap in January, and by then the choice has been made for them.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: In a dispute over a boundary, each neighbour arrives with a memory. One recalls a line of coconut palms planted by his grandfather; the other recalls that the palms were planted inside the line, not on it. Both may be honest. Memory keeps what mattered to the person at the time, and what mattered to the two families was not the same thing.

A survey record does something memory cannot. It was made by a person with no stake in the outcome, at a time when no one was quarrelling, using a method that another surveyor can repeat. These three features, and not the paper or the seal, are what give the record its authority. A document that lacks them is only another memory written down.

This is why the condition of old records deserves more attention than it gets. A map that has faded, a register with a torn page, or an entry corrected in a different ink without initials each reopens the question the record was meant to close. Scanning such documents preserves what survives, but it also fixes every existing error into a form that looks more exact than the original. An officer who reads a crisp digital image should remember that it is a photograph of an old page, and that the page was a person's work on a particular day. Trust in the record is justified. It should stop short of the belief that a record cannot be wrong.

questions.q: According to the first paragraph, what turns visitors from "guests" into "a load"?
opts: A change in the visitors' behaviour
The number arriving compared with what the place can absorb
questions.why: The visitors have not changed; what has changed is the ratio between what arrives and what the place can absorb.

questions.q: Why does the author call carrying capacity "a negotiated figure"?
opts: It is fixed by the State Government
It can be measured exactly with instruments
Setting it involves deciding whose discomfort counts
questions.why: A place has several limits felt differently by different people, so whoever sets the number is choosing whose discomfort counts.

questions.q: The example of the waste plant is used to show that:
opts: a measured limit gives a local body a firm ground for a decision
waste plants should not be built near beaches
panchayats have no power over licences
questions.why: Knowing the plant handles four tonnes a day gives the panchayat a firm reason to refuse a licence that would exceed it.

questions.q: As used in the second paragraph, "awkward" most nearly means:
questions.why: The idea is "simple to state and awkward to apply": easy to say, hard to put into practice.

questions.q: The last two sentences suggest that a place which does not calculate its limits:
opts: will have its limits revealed by shortages and failures
will be fined by the authorities
questions.why: Such places find their limit in the dry tap or the uncollected heap, and by then the choice has been made for them.

questions.q: According to the first paragraph, the two neighbours' accounts differ mainly because:
opts: each family remembered what mattered to it at the time
the palms were replanted after a storm
no survey was ever carried out
questions.why: Both may be honest. Memory keeps what mattered to the person, and that was not the same for the two families.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three features that give a survey record its authority?
opts: It was made by someone with no interest in the outcome
It was made when there was no dispute
It used a method another surveyor can repeat
questions.why: The passage names the three features and adds "and not the paper or the seal".

questions.q: The author's concern about scanning old records is that scanning:
opts: is too costly for small offices
makes existing errors look more exact than they are
questions.why: Scanning "fixes every existing error into a form that looks more exact than the original".

questions.q: As used in the second paragraph, "stake" most nearly means:
opts: a wooden post marking a boundary
questions.why: A person "with no stake in the outcome" has nothing to gain or lose from it.

questions.q: Which statement best expresses the author's view in the last paragraph?
opts: Old records should be discarded once they are scanned
Records deserve trust, but not the belief that they cannot be wrong
Memory is more reliable than a written record
Digital images are more accurate than the originals
questions.why: "Trust in the record is justified. It should stop short of the belief that a record cannot be wrong."

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The file has been pending ______ last Monday.
questions.why: With the present perfect, "since" marks the point in time when something began; "for" is used with a length of time.

questions.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? He did not attend the hearing (A) / because of he (B) / was unwell (C) / on that day (D).
opts: He did not attend the hearing
questions.why: "Because of" is followed by a noun or noun phrase. Before a clause (he was unwell) the word needed is "because".

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: The meeting was postponed, ______?
questions.why: A positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary and tense: was, so wasn't it.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Hardly had the officer left the room ______ the phone rang.
questions.why: "Hardly" and "scarcely" pair with "when". "No sooner" pairs with "than".

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The number of applications received online ______ risen sharply this year.
questions.why: "The number of" takes a singular verb. "A number of" takes a plural verb.

questions.q: Following a Union Home Ministry directive in late 2025, Raj Bhavans, the official residences of Governors, were renamed as:
questions.why: States renamed their Raj Bhavans as Lok Bhavan from late November 2025. Goa's is Lok Bhavan, Dona Paula.

questions.q: Who was elected the 15th Vice President of India in September 2025?
questions.why: C. P. Radhakrishnan defeated B. Sudershan Reddy in the election held on 9 September 2025.

questions.q: Who was sworn in as the 53rd Chief Justice of India on 24 November 2025?
questions.why: Justice Surya Kant succeeded Justice B. R. Gavai, the 52nd Chief Justice.

questions.q: India won its first ICC Women's Cricket World Cup in November 2025 by defeating which team in the final?
questions.why: India beat South Africa by 52 runs in the final at Navi Mumbai on 2 November 2025.

questions.q: Which Indian player won the FIDE Women's World Cup 2025?
questions.why: Divya Deshmukh won the title in July 2025. She was also the only woman to play the open World Cup in Goa later that year.

questions.q: Goa was liberated from Portuguese rule on:
questions.why: 19 December 1961 is observed as Goa Liberation Day. 30 May 1987 is the date of statehood.

questions.q: How many seats are there in the Goa Legislative Assembly?
questions.why: The Goa Legislative Assembly has 40 elected members.

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Minister of Goa, Daman and Diu?
questions.why: Dayanand Bandodkar became Chief Minister after the first elections in 1963.

questions.q: The Fundamental Duties of citizens are set out in which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.why: Article 51A (Part IVA) was inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the State of Goa?
opts: Goa has its own High Court
questions.why: Goa comes under the Bombay High Court, which has a bench at Porvorim.

questions.q: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.why: The gaps grow by one each time: +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6. O is the 15th letter, so the next is the 21st, U.

questions.q: Mamlatdar is to Taluka as Collector is to:
questions.why: A Mamlatdar heads the revenue administration of a taluka; a Collector heads that of a district.

questions.q: Each letter is given its position in the alphabet (A = 1, B = 2, and so on) and a word's value is the sum of its letters, so GOA = 7 + 15 + 1 = 23. What is the value of PANAJI?
Pointing to a woman, Rohan said, "She is the only daughter of my mother's father." How is the woman related to Rohan?
questions.why: His mother's father is his maternal grandfather. That man's only daughter is Rohan's mother.

questions.q: Priya is facing east. She turns 90 degrees clockwise, then 180 degrees, then 90 degrees anticlockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
questions.why: East, then clockwise to south, then about-turn to north, then anticlockwise to west.

questions.q: In a group of 60 candidates, 35 know Konkani, 30 know Marathi and 10 know neither language. How many know both?
questions.why: 50 candidates know at least one language. 35 + 30 - 50 = 15 know both.

questions.q: Five files are stacked one on top of another. The yellow file is above the red one. The red file is above the white one. The white file is above the blue one. The green file is below the blue one. Which file is exactly in the middle?
questions.why: From top to bottom the order is yellow, red, white, blue, green. White is third of five.

questions.q: A train 150 metres long passes a pole in 15 seconds. What is its speed?
questions.why: 150 m in 15 s is 10 m/s, and 10 x 18/5 = 36 km/h. That is not among options A to D.

questions.q: Find the odd one out.
questions.why: 27, 64 and 125 are the cubes of 3, 4 and 5. 144 is a square, not a cube.

questions.q: Statement: "Applicants are advised to bring original documents for verification." Assumptions: I. Some applicants may not bring originals unless they are told to. II. Photocopies are not accepted in any government office.
questions.why: Advice is given because some people might not otherwise follow it, so I is implicit. II goes far beyond this one notice.
